title: Fix checklist state regressions from out-of-order onboarding events (idempotency + monotonic transitions)
author: Logan Wright
release_notes: Prevents checklist steps from regressing when events arrive out of order or are duplicated.
Adds regression coverage for gateway/control-plane reorder scenarios observed during dogfood.
description:
Context: During dogfood we saw checklist steps occasionally "flip backwards" (e.g., "First successful request" completed, then later marked incomplete) when events arrived out of order across gateway/control-plane emitters, or when retries caused duplicates. This manifested most commonly for tenants doing: create API key → immediately test streaming → then make a non-streaming request, where ingestion order is not guaranteed due to async delivery / batching.

What this PR changes: (1) Adds explicit idempotency and ordering semantics to onboarding event ingestion. We now require/derive a stable idempotency key for every event and persist it with a unique constraint per tenant. Duplicates (same tenant_id + idempotency_key) are treated as no-ops. (2) Makes step transitions monotonic. Step state can only move forward (NOT_STARTED → IN_PROGRESS → COMPLETE) and we block regressions even if an older event arrives later. We do still allow explicit Support/admin reset actions (separate path) to move steps backwards, but normal event ingestion will never regress a step. (3) Stores and compares an "event_effective_at" per step to guard against reorder; for server-emitted events we use the server timestamp from the emitter (gateway/control plane) when provided, falling back to ingest time. (4) Adds regression tests that reproduce the exact out-of-order sequences seen in dogfood, including duplicates and mixed streaming/non-streaming.

Implementation notes: - In ChecklistProgressService, per step we now persist: status, first_seen_at, completed_at, last_effective_event_at, and last_effective_event_idempotency_key. The "effective" timestamp is used only to decide whether an incoming event should be allowed to update step fields (e.g., set completed_at) when we receive multiple event types affecting the same step. - Event ingestion endpoint now enforces idempotency via (tenant_id, idempotency_key) uniqueness. For gateway events, idempotency_key is derived from request_id + event_name (request_id already exists in request context); for control-plane events (API key created), idempotency_key uses the control-plane audit event id. If either side fails to provide a stable identifier, we fall back to a generated hash of (event_name, actor_type, actor_id, target_id, emitted_at) with a warning log; this is not ideal but prevents worst-case duplicate amplification.

Tests added: - checklist_progress_out_of_order_test: send STEP_FIRST_2XX complete event, then send older STEP_FIRST_REQUEST_SEEN event; ensure step remains COMPLETE and completed_at does not regress. - checklist_progress_duplicate_event_test: send same gateway event twice; ensure second is ignored and does not change timestamps. - checklist_progress_cross_emitter_reorder_test: API key created (control plane) arrives after first 2xx (gateway) due to delivery delay; ensure both steps end COMPLETE and no state flips.

Operational impact: - Adds a new DB unique index for onboarding_event_dedup (tenant_id, idempotency_key). Migration is included and is safe to run online (index created concurrently; Postgres). - Adds metrics: onboarding_events_deduped_total, onboarding_events_stale_total (events ignored due to older effective time), and checklist_step_regressions_prevented_total. These will help validate we fixed the issue and detect future emitter anomalies.

Risk/rollout: This is behind the existing checklist feature flag and only affects tenants in the dogfood + early cohorts. Worst-case failure mode is we ignore some events deemed "stale"; however, since steps are monotonic, this is preferable to regressing state. Support/admin override remains the escape hatch for truly inconsistent states.

Follow-ups: - Coordinate with Amara Diallo / gateway instrumentation to ensure request_id propagation is always present for onboarding-attributed requests. - Consider enforcing presence of stable idempotency identifiers at the schema level in v1.1 (ADR follow-up) rather than relying on fallback hashing.

Screenshots/logs: Included in the test outputs in CI (see unit test run).

review_conversation: Chloe Martin (request changes): Can we guarantee we never regress step status even if a late event is "in progress"? Also please document how admin reset bypasses monotonic rules. Logan Wright (reply): Updated StepStateMachine to only allow forward transitions on the event path; added explicit reset API path note + unit test for reset path remains allowed (not part of this PR's API surface). Jada Williams (request changes): Unique index needs to be created concurrently; otherwise could lock on bigger tenants even in early cohorts. Logan Wright: Updated migration to CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY and added a note about running migration outside transaction. Caleb Johnson: Add metrics to quantify ignored stale events so we can detect emitter clock skew. Logan Wright: Added onboarding_events_stale_total + label by event_name. Nadia Rahman: Please ensure idempotency_key cardinality is bounded; no raw payload hashing. Logan Wright: Fallback hash uses a bounded set of fields (no prompt/user content) and truncates to 64 chars; also logs warn-level with event_name only. Chloe Martin: LGTM after changes. Caleb Johnson: Approved. Nadia Rahman: Approved.
